paragraphs: Giv sells software to agencies that support people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, covering reporting, scheduling, billing, payroll, electronic health records and electronic medication administration records. The company describes the result as one connected system holding both IDD software and behavioral health software.

The product is organized into hubs, each built around the individual receiving services and tying together care, staff, scheduling and revenue. Records pull EHR, EMR, eMARs and care data into a single view meant to support decisions. Scheduling covers programs, locations and staff in one view. Reports can be produced in seconds using AI that turns agency data into readable insights. Billing tools are aimed at cutting denials and keeping revenue moving. A staff area is meant to keep the team informed and prepared for the day ahead.

The site points to home and community based services as one setting it serves. Skilled nursing for people with IDD is named as another. Agencies moving off another system are told their data, workflows and team will be supported from the first day. The tools are pitched for staff working away from a desk, with real time documentation and visibility on the go.
